## 1. Welcome Series (`WEL`) — Phase 1

**Goal:** Turn a new email subscriber into a first order by helping them pick the right material and size, and by giving them clear reasons to buy their millwork here.

**Trigger:** Profile is added to the Newsletter list (popup, footer form, or account signup with email consent). Klaviyo: List trigger - 'Added to list: Newsletter'.

**Flow filters:**
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow.
- From E2 on: customer_type is not contractor, builder, designer or architect (pros move to Pro Welcome). Build this as a conditional split before E2, E3 and E4 that exits pros, not as a flow filter, so pro-form signups still receive E1 and their code.

**Exits:**
- Places any order, including a samples-only order (Post-Purchase or Sample-to-Order takes over).
- customer_type is set to a pro value: exits at the next pro split (before E2, E3 or E4) and Pro Welcome takes over.
- Unsubscribes from email or is suppressed.

**Smart sending:** Email on (16h) for all four emails, per the cross-flow rule. A brand-new subscriber has no recent sends, so E1 is not at risk; check the 'skipped: Smart Sending' count on E1 after two weeks and raise it if it is more than a handful.

**Branches:**
- **All** Offer path (default): Never ordered before and {{ WELCOME_OFFER }} is live. Gets E1-E4 as written.
- **N** No-offer path: Trigger split at entry: Placed Order at least once over all time (past customers are not eligible for a first-order offer) OR {{ WELCOME_OFFER }} is not confirmed. Sends the alt_versions of E1 and E4; E2 and E3 are the same for everyone.

**KPIs:** Placed order rate (whole flow) → 3-4%; Click rate per email → >= 4%; Material sample orders attributed to E2 → Baseline in first 60 days, then grow; Welcome code redemption rate → Baseline in first 60 days; Pro self-identification clicks in E3 → Track; no target at launch; Unsubscribe rate per email → < 0.5%

**Build notes:**
- Welcome code: {{ welcome_code }} maps to Klaviyo {% coupon_code 'WELCOME' %}. Klaviyo only auto-creates unique codes for platforms it has a coupon integration with; for Miva, plan on creating a batch of single-use, first-order-only codes in Miva and uploading them to Klaviyo as a coupon pool. Confirm with whoever owns the Miva integration.
- Code window: E1 says the code is good for 10 days and E4 (day 8) says it ends in 48 hours, so set the code to expire 10 days after it is issued. E4 must show the same code E1 issued, not a fresh one (a coupon tag issues a new code each time it renders). Options: (a) write the issued code back to a welcome_code profile property via Miva or a webhook and reference that property in E4; (b) use one static WELCOME code with first-order-only and a per-customer 10-day window enforced in Miva. If neither is possible, remove the 48-hour wording from E4 before launch.
- Offer scope: confirm whether the welcome code applies to made-to-order and Design Your Own builder items. The cross-flow guardrail says no percentage off made-to-order items in automated messages unless margin allows. If they are excluded, add 'Excludes made-to-order items.' to the E1 and E4 code callouts (and to SMW-S1). The copy never pairs the code with made-to-order products.
- No-offer path (branch N): trigger split at entry. YES (past customer, or offer not live) sends the E1 and E4 alt_versions. For past customers change 'Your first 5% back' to 'Your next 5% back' in the E4 alt.
- Reply-to: set to cs@architecturaldepot.com. The E1 P.S. invites replies with photos and measurements, and E3 asks for measurements by email.
- Pro links in E3: four links to the homepage carrying ?pro=contractor, ?pro=builder, ?pro=designer and ?pro=architect. Build a small helper flow: trigger = Clicked Email, trigger filter URL contains 'pro=' -> conditional split on the value -> Update Profile Property customer_type. That enters Pro Welcome and exits this flow at the next split. The UTM step must append with '&' because these URLs already carry a '?'. Alternative: point the four links at a Klaviyo-hosted page with a customer_type field.
- Flow priority: Welcome ranks below Post-Purchase, Cart, Sample-to-Order, Depot Dollars, Back in Stock and Browse. Before E2 and E3, add a split 'currently in flow Cart & Checkout Abandonment OR Browse Abandonment' -> YES skips that email. E4 keeps only Smart Sending, because the code deadline matters most to someone who is mid-checkout.
- Samples-only orders count as Placed Order and end this flow (Sample-to-Order takes over). If the business wants the welcome code to survive a sample purchase, change the filter to exclude samples-only orders, and decide whether the code may be used on samples at all.
- E2 sample links: the vinyl shutter color kit links to /LVSAMPLECOLORS.html; a second kit lives at /BESAMPLECOLORS.html. Confirm which shutter line each kit matches and add the second link if both apply.
- Review block in E4: pull a real, published review only. Never write, paraphrase or combine reviews.

### WEL-E3 · Planning help: size it right

*Day 5 - 120 hours after signup (+5d) · EMAIL · branch: All · condition: Not a pro (split exits customer_type = contractor, builder, designer or architect). Skip if currently in Cart & Checkout Abandonment or Browse Abandonment.*

> [Hero image: Hands holding a tape measure up to a kitchen ceiling where a beam will run, painter's tape outlining the beam's width on the drywall, a pencil tucked behind an ear. Natural daylight.]

Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, most sizing mistakes happen before anyone opens a product page. These questions catch them.

**Four questions to answer first**

1. **How long is the run?** Measure wall to wall for beams. For moulding, total every wall and add extra for cuts.
2. **How big should it look?** Tape a paper template where it will go and look from across the room. Size to the space, not the photo.
3. **What's it fastened to?** Know what's behind it: joists, studs or sheathing.
4. **Does it hold anything?** If a corbel or bracket will carry a shelf or counter, call us before you choose one.

**Can't find your size?** Our Design Your Own builders make custom [faux wood beams](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/BM.html), [corbels](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/BUILDER-COR.html), [brackets](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/BUILDER-BKT.html) and [flat trim](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/BUILDER-FLT.html) at off-the-shelf prices. Custom pieces are made to order, so they can't be returned. Double-check your numbers, or send them to us first.

Want a second set of eyes? Call 1-888-573-3768 (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm CT, Sat 8am-12pm CT) or email cs@architecturaldepot.com with your measurements and a photo of the space.

**Are you a pro?** If you're a [contractor](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/?pro=contractor), [builder](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/?pro=builder), [designer](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/?pro=designer) or [architect](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/?pro=architect), click yours and we'll send trade-focused help instead.

**CTA:** [Contact our team](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/HELP.html)

**P.S.** Exterior project? Check that the piece is rated for outdoor use before you order.

## 2. SMS Welcome (`SMW`) — Phase 1

**Goal:** Confirm SMS consent, deliver the SMS welcome code, help with one real decision (seeing the material before buying), and convert before the code expires.

**Trigger:** Consented to SMS from any source (popup step 2, footer form, checkout checkbox, keyword DEPOT, pro form). Klaviyo double opt-in is on, so the profile is added only after replying Y. Klaviyo: List trigger on the SMS subscriber list (fires after double opt-in confirmation).

**Flow filters:**
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow.
- Placed Order zero times over all time. The SMS offer is for first orders; existing customers who opt in still get S0 (a system reply outside this flow) and then skip the flow.
- Has been in this flow zero times over all time, so a STOP and re-join does not issue a second code.
- Can receive SMS marketing (Klaviyo applies this automatically).

**Exits:**
- Places an order.
- Replies STOP (or any opt-out keyword) or is otherwise unsubscribed from SMS.

**Smart sending:** SMS on (24h) for S1-S3. It cannot block S1 for a brand-new subscriber, and S0 is a system reply outside Smart Sending. Quiet hours 10am-8pm recipient local time apply to S1-S3; anything outside the window waits for the next one.

**Branches:**
- **All** All new SMS subscribers: No split. Optional S2 variant for shutter browsers is in build_notes.

**KPIs:** Click rate per SMS → >= 8%; Placed order rate (whole flow) → 4-5%; SMS welcome code redemption rate → Baseline in first 60 days; Opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%; Double opt-in completion rate (replied Y / prompted) → >= 70%

**Build notes:**
- S0 is not a flow message: paste its text into Klaviyo SMS settings as the opt-in confirmation reply. It is listed here so the whole welcome sequence reads in one place. The double opt-in prompt itself lives in the SMS program doc.
- SMS code: {{ welcome_code }} here is a separate coupon from the email welcome code (e.g. WELCOME_SMS) that expires 7 days after it is issued, so 'Expires in 7 days' in S1 and 'ends tomorrow' in S3 (day 6) are both true. S3 must show the code S1 issued, not a new one; use the same solution chosen for WEL-E4 (code written back to a profile property, or a static code with a per-customer window in Miva). Set both email and SMS codes to single-use and first-order-only so only one applies.
- Offer scope: if the welcome code excludes made-to-order items, change S1 to '...with code {{ welcome_code }} (excl. made-to-order).' and re-check length.
- Rendered length: {{ WELCOME_OFFER }} renders as '10% off your first order' (24 characters vs 19 literal) and a unique code is usually 8-12 characters (vs 18 literal), so S1 and S3 still land in one 160-character segment. Re-check if the offer wording gets longer.
- Frequency cap: S1, S2 and S3 are 3 marketing texts inside 7 days, which is the whole cap on their own. Exclude profiles currently in this flow from SMS campaigns until day 7. Before S2 and S3, add a split: received 3 or more marketing texts in the last 7 days -> skip. If something has to give, skip S2 and keep S3.
- Send times: S1 immediately after confirmation (quiet hours may hold a late-evening opt-in until 10am). S2 on day 2 at 2pm recipient local time. S3 on day 6 at 11am recipient local time. The phone line in S3 is staffed Mon-Fri 8am-6pm CT and Sat 8am-12pm CT; a Sunday send is fine because the code is the point.
- Optional S2 variant for profiles who viewed a shutter product in the last 30 days (conditional split on Viewed Product category): 'Architectural Depot: Matching shutters to siding? Try a vinyl shutter color sample kit against the house: {link} Reply STOP to opt out' linking to https://www.architecturaldepot.com/LVSAMPLECOLORS.html (151 characters with the link).
- Links: Klaviyo shortens {link} with the branded domain; one link per text, no other shorteners.

## 3. Cart & Checkout Abandonment (`CRT`) — Phase 1

**Goal:** Recover started checkouts by answering the questions that stall a millwork order (size, material, delivery, returns, install), giving high-value carts a real person and made-to-order carts an honest, reassuring note.

**Trigger:** Started Checkout (Klaviyo metric trigger from the Miva integration). Fallback: Added to Cart, if Miva cannot send Started Checkout.

**Flow filters:**
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow
- Has not been in this flow in the last 7 days
- Can receive email marketing; SMS steps also require SMS consent

**Exits:**
- Placed Order (any order): exits immediately, all branches
- Unsubscribes from email (email steps stop) or replies STOP (SMS steps stop)

**Smart sending:** Email: OFF for CRT-E1 so it lands about an hour after checkout (the cross-flow exception); ON (16h) for CRT-E2, CRT-E2A, CRT-E2B and CRT-E3. SMS: ON (24h), quiet hours 10am-8pm recipient local time, counts toward the 3-per-7-days SMS cap.

**Branches:**
- **A** High-value cart: Started Checkout value >= $1,000. Checked first, so a high-value cart with made-to-order items lands here (the specialist note covers made-to-order).
- **B** Made-to-order in cart: Checkout value < $1,000 AND at least one item flagged made-to-order (vinyl shutters, wood shutters, Design Your Own builder items, other made-to-order SKUs).
- **Default** Everyone else: Checkout value < $1,000 and no made-to-order items.

**KPIs:** Placed order rate (per recipient, whole flow) → 6%; Email click rate → 7%; Branch A reply or call rate (CRT-E2A) → 5%; SMS click rate → 10%; Revenue per recipient → Set baseline in first 30 days, then +10% per quarter; Email unsubscribe rate → < 0.3%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**
- Started Checkout must carry: line items (name, SKU, image, URL, size/options, quantity, price), checkout $value, and a per-item made-to-order flag (e.g. is_made_to_order from a Miva product custom field). Without the flag, branch B can't be built; route those carts to Default until it exists.
- {{ cart_url }} must restore the cart on any device (a Miva basket-restore or checkout URL passed on the event). If none exists, fall back to https://www.architecturaldepot.com/BASK.html, which only works in the same browser.
- Split order: CRT-E1 and CRT-S1 sit above the splits. Before E2, split 1 on value >= 1000 (A), then split 2 on made-to-order (B), else Default. Klaviyo paths don't rejoin, so duplicate CRT-E3 and CRT-S2 into each path with identical content and ids.
- CRT-E1's 'Made-to-order pieces in your cart' callout is a show/hide block: show only when the cart has a made-to-order item. Its copy is written conditionally, so it still reads correctly if shown to everyone.
- CRT-E2A is a plain-text template: no header, nav or images (keep the required footer). From name: '{{ SPECIALIST_NAME }} at Architectural Depot'. Reply-to must be a monitored inbox (the specialist's or cs@architecturaldepot.com), answered within one business day. Confirm a real, named person before launch; swap in a direct extension if they have one.
- {{ CART_INCENTIVE }} is optional and needs approval before launch. If approved: bonus Depot Dollars only (never a percentage off, never a discount on made-to-order items), valid 48 hours from CRT-E3, credited once the order ships. Set a profile property (cart_incentive_expires) so CS can honor it. If not approved, send CRT-E3's no-incentive version.
- CRT-S2 is written without the incentive. If {{ CART_INCENTIVE }} is approved, swap to: 'Architectural Depot: Last reminder: order your saved cart in the next 48 hrs to earn [incentive in plain words]. {link} Reply STOP to opt out' and keep it under 160 characters, GSM-7 only.
- SMS steps: condition SMS consent = subscribed; quiet hours 10am-8pm local (a text that falls outside waits for the next window).
- No 'not in Post-Purchase' filter on purpose: Klaviyo removes a profile the moment it fails a flow filter, so that filter would cancel cart recovery for any repeat buyer within 3 weeks of an order. Smart Sending (16h) spaces Cart and Post-Purchase emails instead.

## 4. Browse Abandonment (`BRW`) — Phase 1

**Goal:** Turn a product view into a confident next step (the right size, a material sample or a quick call) without discounting, and help Design Your Own visitors finish their custom piece.

**Trigger:** Viewed Product (Klaviyo metric from onsite tracking / the Miva integration). Design Your Own builder pages (/BUILDER-COR.html, /BUILDER-BKT.html, /BUILDER-FLT.html, /BM.html) must also fire Viewed Product, or a custom 'Viewed Builder' event, so they route to branch C.

**Flow filters:**
- Started Checkout zero times since starting this flow
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow
- Has not been in this flow in the last 14 days
- Is not currently in the Cart flow
- Is not currently in the Post-Purchase, Sample-to-Order, Depot Dollars or Back in Stock flows (all outrank Browse)
- Can receive email marketing; BRW-S1 also requires SMS consent

**Exits:**
- Started Checkout: exits (the Cart flow takes over)
- Placed Order: exits
- Unsubscribes from email (email steps stop) or replies STOP (SMS steps stop)

**Smart sending:** Email ON (16h). SMS ON (24h), quiet hours 10am-8pm local, counts toward the 3-per-7-days SMS cap.

**Branches:**
- **C** Custom builder: Triggering view is a Design Your Own builder page: URL contains /BUILDER- (corbels, brackets, flat trim) or is /BM.html (faux wood beams).
- **Default** Standard product: Any other product page.

**KPIs:** Placed order rate (per recipient) → 1.5%; Email click rate → 5%; Sample orders from flow (per recipient) → 0.5%; Branch C placed order rate → 2%; SMS click rate (BRW-S1) → 8%; Email unsubscribe rate → < 0.3%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**
- Viewed Product payload needs: ProductName, ProductID, URL, ImageURL, Price, Categories and an is_made_to_order flag. {{ category_name }} maps to the primary category with fallback 'millwork' (the subject then reads 'Still planning your millwork project?').
- Branch C: add the Klaviyo onsite snippet to the builder pages so they send Viewed Product with the page URL and a builder_type property (beam, corbel, bracket, flat trim). If they can only send a custom event, build branch C as its own flow on that event with the same filters, and add 'has not been in Browse (custom) in the last 14 days' to the standard flow.
- For branch C, {{ product_url }} is the builder page they viewed. Builder entries may not be saved between visits, so the copy never promises a saved design.
- BRW-E1's 'If it's made to order' callout is a show/hide block: show only when the viewed product is made to order (e.g. vinyl or wood shutters).
- BRW-E2 recommendations: Klaviyo catalog feed, same category as the viewed product, in stock, excluding the viewed item. Swap the hero image by category with show/hide image blocks (beams, corbels, shutters, mantels, moulding, other).
- BRW-E2 review block: pull a real review for the viewed category from the customer reviews page. If none exists for that category, use a real review about help choosing size or finish. Quote verbatim.
- BRW-S1 condition: Klaviyo splits can't match against the trigger's product, so either (a) send a site-side 'Repeat Viewed Product' event when the same product is viewed 2+ times in 7 days and split on it, or (b) approximate with 'Viewed Product at least 3 times in the last 7 days'. Prefer (a).
- BRW-S1 sends at day 1 in both branches (it sits above the branch split).

## 5. Post-Purchase (`PP`) — Phase 1

**Goal:** Turn every order into a well-installed project and a second order: set honest expectations, help them prep and install, ask for a review once it's up, then suggest the pieces that finish the job.

**Trigger:** Placed Order (Klaviyo metric trigger from the Miva integration). Trigger filter: is_samples_only = false, so samples-only orders go to Sample-to-Order instead.

**Flow filters:**
- Order is not samples-only (is_samples_only = false). Samples-only orders enter Sample-to-Order.
- Placed Order (non-sample) zero times since starting this flow. A newer order ends this run and starts a fresh one in the repeat branch, so nobody gets two parallel sequences.
- Country is not Canada OR email consent is subscribed (CASL). US buyers who never subscribed can receive these under CAN-SPAM.
- SMS steps only: can receive SMS marketing (consented).

**Exits:**
- Places another non-sample order: this run ends and the new order starts a new run (repeat branch).
- Order cancelled or fully refunded, if Miva sends a Cancelled Order or Refunded Order event.
- Unsubscribes from email (email steps) or texts STOP (SMS steps).

**Smart sending:** E1 variants (PP-E1, PP-E1R, PP-E1M): Smart Sending OFF, because they are order-specific and should always arrive. All other emails ON (16h). SMS ON (24h), quiet hours 10am-8pm local, max 3 marketing texts per rolling 7 days.

**Branches:**
- **F** First order, in-stock only: Placed Order where is_samples_only = false equals 1 time over all time (this order) AND has_made_to_order = false
- **R** Repeat order, in-stock only: Placed Order where is_samples_only = false at least 2 times over all time AND has_made_to_order = false
- **M** Contains made-to-order: has_made_to_order = true (any order count). Gets PP-E1M, and E3, S2 and E4 wait until the order has shipped.

**KPIs:** E1 click rate (all variants) → 6% (starting benchmark; reset after 60 days of data); Review page clicks per recipient (E3 + S2) → 4%; Repeat order rate within 90 days of entry → Baseline in month 1, then +10% relative; E4 revenue per recipient → Baseline in month 1, then grow; Unsubscribe rate per email → < 0.3%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**
- Data: the Placed Order event must carry line items with SKU, product name, category, image URL, product URL and a made_to_order flag, plus order-level booleans is_samples_only and has_made_to_order. If Miva has no made_to_order flag, derive it from category/SKU: vinyl shutters, wood shutters, Design Your Own builder items (BUILDER-COR, BUILDER-BKT, BUILDER-FLT, BM) and made-to-order faux wood beams.
- Structure: Trigger > conditional split on has_made_to_order. YES = M path (PP-E1M). NO = second split on non-sample order count >= 2: YES = R path (PP-E1R), NO = F path (PP-E1). Klaviyo branches do not rejoin, so clone the tail (S1, E2, E3, S2, E4) into each path with identical content. Each customer receives 4 emails and up to 2 texts; the file holds 6 emails because E1 has three variants.
- PP-E1M is shared by first and repeat made-to-order orders, so its copy works for both. Optional: add a show/hide line 'Good to see you again.' for repeat customers.
- M path timing: E3, S2 and E4 must not ask for a review or push add-ons before a made-to-order piece has even shipped. Preferred build: if Miva sends a shipment event (Fulfilled Order / Shipped), end the M path after E2 and run its E3, S2 and E4 from a small clone flow triggered on that event with has_made_to_order = true (E3 10 days after shipment, S2 1 day later, E4 7 days after E3). Fallback: set the M-path delay before E3 to the confirmed {{ MTO_LEAD_TIME }} plus 14 days.
- Do not duplicate the storefront's transactional order and shipping confirmations. No order totals, tracking numbers or addresses in these emails; refer to the confirmations instead.
- PP-S1 link: defaults to /HELP.html. If the Placed Order event carries product URLs, link the first line item's product page instead, since that is where its installation guide and specs live.
- PP-E2 category tips block: one short tip per purchased category, written from the Ekena installation guides and approved by customer service before launch. Safe starters: Beams - find the joists and confirm the mounting method in the guide before marking beam lines. Shutters - measure every window; follow the guide's fastening method for your siding. Corbels and brackets - check the specs before anything rests on them. Mantels - follow the guide and your local code for clearances around the fireplace. Columns - confirm in the specs whether the column is decorative or structural. Moulding and trim - plan corners and joints and dry-fit first. Ceiling medallions - turn off power at the breaker before working around a light fixture. No invented specs, cure times or load ratings.
- PP-E3 and PP-S2 review link: the store reviews page (/architecturaldepot-customer-reviews.html). If a product-review app is connected later, swap to its per-product review form. Do not gate reviews: everyone gets the same ask, happy or not.
- PP-S2 condition: skip anyone who clicked the review link in PP-E3 (Clicked Email where URL contains 'customer-reviews' since starting flow). If the review platform sends a Submitted Review event, use that instead.
- PP-E3: if {{ INSTAGRAM_HANDLE }} is not confirmed at launch, delete the sentence that mentions it rather than shipping the token.
- PP-E4 cross-sell map (products block): corbels > shelf brackets, mantels; beams > beam straps, brackets, corbels; shutters > SteelTek shutter hardware; mantels > corbels, moulding; columns > balustrade railing kits; moulding and trim > ceiling medallions. ## 6. Depot Dollars Expiring (`DD`) — Phase 2

**Goal:** Get customers to spend their Depot Dollars before they expire by reminding them of the balance, showing small pieces it can go toward and explaining how to apply it at checkout.

**Trigger:** Date-based: Klaviyo date-property trigger on the profile property depot_dollars_expiration_date. Hour 0 = the expiry date; messages go out 14, 3 and 2 days before it. Requires a Miva -> Klaviyo sync of depot_dollars_balance and depot_dollars_expiration_date. Until that sync exists, use the fallback: Klaviyo metric trigger Placed Order, with the first message 76 days after the order.

**Flow filters:**
- depot_dollars_balance > 0 (when synced). Klaviyo re-checks flow filters before every message, so a balance that is spent or expires stops the flow.
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow.
- Fallback build only: no balance is available to filter on, so the Placed Order filter does the work. A newer order removes the profile from the older order's reminders and starts its own run.

**Exits:**
- Places any order (flow filter). Post-Purchase takes over, and its E4 already says the new Depot Dollars are ready.
- depot_dollars_balance drops to 0 because the balance was used or has expired.
- The expiry date passes. E2, 2 days before, is the last message.
- Unsubscribes from email: the email steps stop but S1 still sends if SMS-consented. Replies STOP: S1 is skipped but the emails still send.

**Smart sending:** Email on (16h) / SMS on (24h). This is the program default. DD ranks below Post-Purchase, Cart and Sample-to-Order, so if one of those sent within the window, this reminder gives way. If Smart Sending skips E2, SMS subscribers already got the date in S1.

**Branches:**
- **All** Everyone with an expiring balance: No split. The fallback build (Placed Order + 76 days) uses the no-balance alt versions of E1 and E2 and the fallback S1 text in build_notes.

**KPIs:** Placed order rate before expiry (per recipient) → 5% (starting benchmark; reset after 60 days of data); Share of expiring Depot Dollars redeemed before expiry → Set a baseline in the first 60 days, then +25%; Email click rate → 4%; SMS click rate → 8%; Email unsubscribe rate per send → < 0.3%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**
- Data (required for the full build): sync two profile properties from Miva to Klaviyo at least daily, and again after every order, shipment and Depot Dollars redemption. (1) depot_dollars_expiration_date: the last day the soonest-expiring unspent Depot Dollars can be used, stored as a date. (2) depot_dollars_balance: the amount expiring on that date, formatted as currency with the dollar sign (e.g. $37.50). Every subject, SMS and headline assumes the token renders with the $ sign. Show the date in a readable format such as 'October 19'.
- If Miva can only provide the total balance (not the amount expiring on the next date), tell the copy owner. For customers whose Depot Dollars come from more than one order, 'Your $X expires on [date]' would then overstate what is expiring, and the lines need to read 'Some of your $X in Depot Dollars expires on [date]'.
- Trigger setup: a one-time Klaviyo date-property flow on depot_dollars_expiration_date (not set to repeat annually). Hour 0 = expiry date. DD-E1 goes out 14 days before at 10am local (offset_hours -336), DD-S1 3 days before at 11am local (-72) and DD-E2 2 days before at 10am local (-48). The profile qualifies again whenever the property moves to a new date after a later order.
- Fallback until the sync exists: metric trigger Placed Order. E1 goes out 76 days after the order, S1 after 87 days and E2 after 88 days. Depot Dollars become available when the order ships and expire 90 days after they are earned, so the real expiry is on or after order date + 90 and fallback reminders arrive early, never late. Use the alt_versions of E1 and E2 (no balance or date tokens) and this S1 text: 'Architectural Depot: The Depot Dollars from your last order expire soon. Use them at checkout: {link} Reply STOP to opt out'.
- Checkout mechanics: verify before launch. DD-E2 step 2 assumes the balance appears when the customer checks out signed in to the account that earned it, and step 3 assumes they apply it during checkout. Confirm with the Miva setup whether sign-in is required and whether Depot Dollars apply automatically or must be selected, then adjust steps 2 and 3 if needed.
- The small-item cards (finials, plinth blocks, ceiling medallions, samples, shutter hardware) are ideas, not prices. Never show prices or 'free' language next to them, because balances vary and an item can cost more than the balance. Only the sample card links out, to the verified /BM-MAT-SAMPLE.html. Add category links for the other cards once their URLs are verified.
- Priority: DD ranks below Post-Purchase, Cart and Sample-to-Order. Rely on Smart Sending for collisions and do not add 'not in flow X' filters here, because a flow filter would remove the profile from the rest of the reminder sequence.
- SMS: DD-S1 goes out at 11am recipient local time, inside the 10am-8pm quiet-hours window, and counts toward the 3-per-rolling-7-days cap. With literal tokens the text is 160 characters. With a real balance and date it renders at about 125.
- Images: use real Ekena product photography. The balance and date are always live HTML text and are never baked into an image.

## 7. Sample-to-Order (`SMP`) — Phase 2

**Goal:** Turn a sample order into a confident full order by teaching them how to judge the sample, pointing them to the matching line and custom sizes, and getting their measurements in front of a real person.

**Trigger:** Placed Order (Klaviyo metric trigger from the Miva integration) where every line item is a sample: trigger filter is_samples_only = true (all SKUs contain SAMPLE, e.g. SAMPLE-URETHANE, BM-MAT-SAMPLE, LVSAMPLECOLORS, BESAMPLECOLORS, moulding profile samples).

**Flow filters:**
- Placed Order where is_samples_only = false zero times since starting this flow.
- Currently in flow Post-Purchase is false (Post-Purchase outranks).
- Has not been in this flow in the last 30 days, so a second sample order does not restart the sequence.
- SMS step only: can receive SMS marketing (consented).

**Exits:**
- Places a non-sample order (Placed Order where is_samples_only = false). They move to Post-Purchase.
- Unsubscribes from email (email steps) or texts STOP (SMS step).

**Smart sending:** Email ON (16h). SMS ON (24h), quiet hours 10am-8pm local, max 3 marketing texts per rolling 7 days. E1 can stay on: the storefront's transactional confirmation is not a Klaviyo marketing send, so it does not block E1.

**Branches:**
- **All** All sample orders: No split. Products blocks, the E2 CTA and the S1 link adapt to the sampled line by SKU (map in build_notes).

**KPIs:** Sample-to-order conversion (non-sample order within 45 days of entry) → 15% (starting benchmark; reset after 60 days of data); Email click rate → 4%; Revenue per recipient → Baseline in month 1, then grow; Calls or emails to CS citing samples (tag in the help desk) → Track; no target at launch; Unsubscribe rate per email → < 0.3%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**

Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, thanks for ordering samples. It's the smart first step in a millwork project, because color, grain and texture never look quite the same on a screen as they do in your space. Your shipping confirmation will have the tracking. When they arrive, try this:

**Your samples**

> [Dynamic products × 4: Dynamic: sample line items from the Placed Order event (image and name), each linked to its sample page.]

**How to judge a sample**

1. **See it in your light** Look in the morning, mid-afternoon and at night under your lamps. Color reads differently in each.
2. **Hold it where it will go** Up at the ceiling for a beam, beside the window for a shutter, along the wall for moulding. Then step back across the room.
3. **Compare it with what's staying** Set it next to your floors, cabinets, trim, brick or paint.
4. **Feel the texture** Run a hand over the grain. That's what you'll see up close every day.
5. **Snap a photo** Take one in place to share with whoever helps you decide.

Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }}, once you've picked a material, size is the next big decision. Here's what to have on paper before you order. Treat it as a starting point; each product page lists the exact specs.

**What to measure**

- **Ceiling beams** — Room length and width, ceiling height, which way the joists run, and how many beams you're picturing.
- **Shutters** — Height and width of every window opening. Measure each one, even if they look identical.
- **Mantels and corbels** — Width and height of the wall or fireplace, and what the piece will hold. Check the specs before anything rests on it.
- **Moulding and trim** — Length of each wall, ceiling height, and a count of inside and outside corners.
- **Columns** — Floor-to-ceiling height, and whether it's decorative or needs to carry weight. The specs will tell you.

**Get a second set of eyes**

1. **Sketch it** A rough drawing with dimensions is plenty.
2. **Take two photos** One wide shot of the space, one close-up of where it mounts.
3. **Send or call** Email cs@architecturaldepot.com or call 1-888-573-3768 and we'll walk through sizes with you.

**CTA:** [Get planning help](https://www.architecturaldepot.com/HELP.html)

## 9. Back in Stock + Price Drop (`BIS`) — Phase 2

**Goal:** Tell shoppers the moment an item they wanted is available again or costs less, and help them order the right size with confidence.

**Trigger:** Branch A: Subscribed to Back in Stock (Klaviyo catalog back-in-stock; messages go out when Klaviyo sees the item restocked). Branch B: Klaviyo Price Drop trigger on an item the profile viewed or added to cart in the last 30 days (requires catalog sync with prices).

**Flow filters:**
- BIS-E1A and BIS-S1A: no priority suppression beyond consent, because the shopper asked for this alert
- BIS-E2A: Placed Order zero times since starting this flow; not currently in the Cart or Post-Purchase flows
- Branch B: Placed Order zero times since starting; not currently in the Post-Purchase, Cart, Sample-to-Order or Depot Dollars flows (all outrank Back in Stock); has not been in branch B in the last 7 days
- Can receive email marketing; SMS steps also require SMS consent

**Exits:**
- Placed Order: exits
- Unsubscribes from email (email steps stop) or replies STOP (SMS steps stop)

**Smart sending:** BIS-E1A and BIS-S1A: Smart Sending OFF, because the shopper asked for this alert and it should arrive when the item is back (SMS still waits for quiet hours, 10am-8pm local). Everything else: email ON (16h), SMS ON (24h).

**Branches:**
- **A** Back in stock: Subscribed to Back in Stock for an item; sends when the Klaviyo catalog shows inventory above the restock threshold.
- **B** Price drop: Catalog price drops (by at least the agreed minimum) on an item the profile viewed or added to cart in the last 30 days.

**KPIs:** Branch A placed order rate (per recipient) → 8%; Branch A email click rate → 15%; Branch B placed order rate (per recipient) → 3%; Branch B email click rate → 6%; SMS click rate → 12%; Email unsubscribe rate → < 0.3%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**
- Build as two Klaviyo flows that share the BIS code and reporting tag: 'BIS-A Back in Stock' (trigger: Subscribed to Back in Stock) and 'BIS-B Price Drop' (trigger: Price Drop).
- Branch A needs: a Klaviyo catalog synced from Miva with inventory quantity; the Klaviyo back-in-stock form on out-of-stock product pages (email, plus optional SMS opt-in with the compliant disclosure from the SMS program doc); and back-in-stock settings (restock threshold, batch size) agreed with operations so alerts don't oversell what came in.
- Made-to-order items are built to order and rarely show as out of stock, so branch A is mostly in-stock lines. Branch B can include made-to-order items, so BIS-E1B carries the made-to-order line as a show/hide bullet (show when is_made_to_order = true).
- Branch B: Klaviyo Price Drop with a 30-day lookback on Viewed Product and Added to Cart. Agree a minimum drop with the business so tiny changes don't fire. Only real, standing catalog prices; QA the feed so a pricing error never triggers a send.
- BIS-E1B shows previous and new prices exactly as the catalog supplies them. Do not compute or show a percent-off badge (made-to-order discount guardrail).
- BIS-S1B goes only to profiles who added the item to cart: split on the Price Drop trigger's source event if Klaviyo exposes it; otherwise approximate with 'Added to Cart at least once in the last 30 days'.
- BIS-E2A: skip it if the item is out of stock again at send time (catalog inventory check). If that can't be automated, the similar-pieces block keeps the email useful.
- SMS: quiet hours 10am-8pm local; BIS-S1A waits for the next window if a restock lands overnight.


### BIS-E1A · It's back in stock

*Immediately when the item is restocked (+0h) · EMAIL · branch: A · condition: Branch A: item restocked (Klaviyo back-in-stock)*

## 10. Win-Back (`WIN`) — Phase 3

**Goal:** Bring past customers back for their next millwork project with ideas, what's new and help that answers their questions, and be honest about emailing less if they aren't ready.

**Trigger:** Segment-triggered (Klaviyo 'Added to segment'): the profile enters the 'Lapsed customers' segment. The segment is Placed Order at least once over all time AND Placed Order zero times in the last 180 days AND Active on Site zero times in the last 60 days. For pros (customer_type is contractor, builder, designer or architect) the window is zero times in the last 120 days.

**Flow filters:**
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow.
- Has been in Cart & Checkout Abandonment (CRT), Browse Abandonment (BRW), Back in Stock + Price Drop (BIS), Sample-to-Order (SMP) and Depot Dollars Expiring (DD) zero times since starting this flow. If they're back on the site, the higher-priority flow takes over.
- Has been in this flow zero times in the last 365 days.

**Exits:**
- Places any order.
- Enters a higher-priority flow (CRT, BRW, BIS, SMP or DD).
- Unsubscribes from email: the email steps stop but WIN-S1 still sends if SMS-consented. Replies STOP: S1 is skipped but the emails still send.
- Completes WIN-E3. Profiles that don't click move to the lower-frequency campaign segment described in build_notes.

**Smart sending:** Email on (16h) / SMS on (24h). This is the program default. Win-Back is near the bottom of the priority order, so it should always give way to higher-priority flows.

**Branches:**
- **All** All lapsed customers: No split. Pros enter on a 120-day site-inactivity window instead of 60, which is set in the segment. Each email step has a conditional split that skips profiles with email_sunset = true.

**KPIs:** Reactivation rate (order within 30 days of entry) → 3% (starting benchmark; reset after 90 days of data); Email click rate → 2.5%; SMS click rate → 6%; Revenue per recipient → Set a baseline in the first 90 days; Email unsubscribe rate per send → < 0.5%; SMS opt-out rate per send → < 1.5%

**Build notes:**
- Segment 'Lapsed customers': (Placed Order at least once over all time) AND (Placed Order zero times in the last 180 days) AND ((customer_type is not in [contractor, builder, designer, architect] AND Active on Site zero times in the last 60 days) OR (customer_type is in [contractor, builder, designer, architect] AND Active on Site zero times in the last 120 days)). Active on Site needs Klaviyo's onsite tracking on the Miva storefront. If that isn't live, substitute Viewed Product zero times over the same windows.
- Re-entry: a customer should go through Win-Back at most once every 365 days (flow filter). Confirm how Klaviyo handles re-entry for segment-triggered flows. If profiles can't re-enter, rebuild the trigger as a scheduled check or clone the flow each year.
- Depot Dollars: everyone in this flow last ordered 180+ days ago, and Depot Dollars expire 90 days after they're earned, so their earned balance has expired. Never say 'you have Depot Dollars' and never show {{ depot_dollars_balance }} here. The copy only talks about what the next order earns (5% back).
- {{ WINBACK_INCENTIVE }} (default 'bonus Depot Dollars') appears only in WIN-E3. Before launch, set the amount, an end date, exclusions and how bonus Depot Dollars are issued in Miva (manual credit, coupon or rule). If you add an end date, add it to the E3 callout. Under the discount guardrails, never use a percentage off on made-to-order items (vinyl and wood shutters, Design Your Own builder items, made-to-order beams). If the incentive is not approved, send the E3 no-incentive alt version.
- Make E3's 'we'll write less often' promise true. After E3, wait 7 days, then use a conditional split on Clicked Email zero times since starting this flow AND Placed Order zero times since starting. On the YES path, use Update Profile Property winback_low_frequency = true. Recommendation: campaign segments send these profiles major sales and new-product launches only (about 2 a month). Clear the property when they click, visit or order. If they stay unengaged, the Sunset flow takes over at 120 days.
- email_sunset: put a conditional split before each email (email_sunset is not true). Sunset profiles skip the emails but can still get WIN-S1 if SMS-consented.
- WIN-E2 products block: needs a 'new' tag or a created date in the Klaviyo catalog feed. If neither exists, replace the block with Klaviyo's 'recommended for you' feed for the category they bought before, and change the block title to 'Picked for your next project'.
- What's new is limited to verified items: the new generation of Timberthane faux wood ('even more realistic, still maintenance-free'), wall and ceiling motif kits, slat wall kits, new shutter styles and SteelTek hardware. Don't add sizes, finishes, prices or launch dates unless they're pulled from the live product pages. Point the kit and shutter cards at their category pages once those URLs are verified. For now they go to /ekena-millwork.html.
- SMS: WIN-S1 goes out on day 10 at 1pm recipient local time, inside the 10am-8pm quiet-hours window, and counts toward the 3-per-rolling-7-days cap. It carries no incentive.
- Images: real Ekena product photography only. The E1 hero should feature new-generation Timberthane beams.

## 11. Sunset / Re-engagement (`SUN`) — Phase 3

**Goal:** Ask unengaged subscribers whether they still want our emails. Keep the ones who say yes, and quietly stop campaign sends to the ones who don't answer, to protect inbox placement for everyone else.

**Trigger:** Segment-triggered (Klaviyo 'Added to segment'): the profile enters the 'Unengaged 120d' segment. The segment is Clicked Email zero times in the last 120 days AND Active on Site zero times in the last 120 days AND Received Email at least 8 times in the last 120 days AND can receive email marketing. Opens are deliberately not used, because Apple Mail Privacy Protection inflates them.

**Flow filters:**
- Clicked Email zero times since starting this flow.
- Active on Site zero times since starting this flow.
- Placed Order zero times since starting this flow.
- Has been in Win-Back (WIN) zero times in the last 30 days, because Win-Back outranks Sunset.
- email_sunset is not true.

**Exits:**
- Clicks any link in either email, including 'Keep me subscribed'. They stay fully subscribed and email_sunset is never set.
- Visits the site or places an order.
- Updates their choices on the Klaviyo preference page ('fewer emails'). See build_notes.
- Unsubscribes.
- Day 12 with no click: email_sunset = true is set and the profile leaves the flow. It is not unsubscribed.

**Smart sending:** Email on (16h). This is the program default, and Sunset is last in the priority order. Email only: this flow never sends SMS and never changes SMS consent.

**Branches:**
- **All** All unengaged email subscribers: No split.

**KPIs:** Re-engagement rate (clicked any SUN email) → 5% (starting benchmark; reset after 90 days of data); Spam complaint rate per send → < 0.1%; Unsubscribe rate per send → Track it. A higher rate than other flows is expected and healthy here.; Share of entrants set to email_sunset = true → Track monthly; Campaign click rate after sunset exclusion → Higher than the 30 days before launch

**Build notes:**
- Exact post-flow step: after SUN-E2, add a 7-day time delay (day 12, offset_hours 288 from the trigger). Then add a conditional split: Clicked Email zero times since starting this flow AND Active on Site zero times since starting this flow AND Placed Order zero times since starting this flow AND has not updated preferences since starting this flow. YES path: Update Profile Property email_sunset = true, then end. NO path: end with no change. After 7 more days with no click, the profile has email_sunset = true and is excluded from campaign segments. Add 'email_sunset is not true' to the master sendable/engaged segment that every campaign audience is built from, or to each campaign audience if there is no master segment. Do not unsubscribe or suppress these profiles.
- Segment 'Unengaged 120d': Clicked Email zero times in the last 120 days AND Active on Site zero times in the last 120 days AND Received Email at least 8 times in the last 120 days AND can receive email marketing. Never use Opened Email. Active on Site needs Klaviyo's onsite tracking on the Miva storefront.
- Keep me subscribed: the link registers a click, and any click removes the profile from the flow and from the segment. It points to the verified /blogs/ page because the email offers project ideas. Optional: build a short 'You're still subscribed' landing page and swap the URL. Mark that new path for verification.
- Fewer emails: set up the Klaviyo preference page with topic or frequency choices (for example project ideas, new products, sales). Anyone who submits it has answered, so exclude them from the day-12 sunset step. Do this with the 'has not updated preferences' condition: a list or property change made by the preference page since the flow started.
- Tags: {% manage_preferences %} and {% unsubscribe %} render as complete links in Klaviyo. If the template needs a bare URL (for a card or button href), use the URL versions of these tags. Check Klaviyo's template tag reference for the exact names. Klaviyo may not count clicks on these two links as Clicked Email. That's fine: an unsubscribe ends the flow, and a preference update is handled by the condition above.
- What email_sunset = true means: excluded from campaigns only. Flows that react to new activity (Browse, Cart, Back in Stock, Post-Purchase, Sample-to-Order) still send, because new activity means they're engaged again. Win-Back email steps skip email_sunset = true. SMS is unaffected.
- Reactivation: build a small utility flow triggered by Active on Site, Placed Order or Clicked Email, filtered to email_sunset = true, with one action: Update Profile Property email_sunset = false. This lets returning customers back into campaigns automatically.
- While a profile is in this flow (days 0-12), exclude it from campaigns ('Has been in flow SUN zero times in the last 12 days' in the master sendable segment), so the check-in is the only email they get from us in that window.
- No offers, discounts or product grids in this flow. The point is an honest question, not one more sale email.
- Optional, a business decision: profiles that stay email_sunset = true for 365 days with no activity can be suppressed to reduce Klaviyo profile costs. Don't do it automatically without sign-off.
